# Neural Radiance Fields and Implicit Neural Representations

Also called: INR-based Tomography, Neural Volume Rendering for CT

## Overview
This family applies Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) to tomographic reconstruction, replacing discrete voxel grids with continuous functions parameterized by neural networks [S1, unofficial]. It solves the ill-posed inverse problem of recovering 3D density fields from sparse, noisy, or limited-angle X-ray projections by leveraging the differentiability of the rendering pipeline [S1, unofficial]. Unlike traditional discrete methods, these approaches optimize network weights directly, allowing for high-resolution reconstruction from minimal data and enabling simultaneous self-calibration of geometric and photometric parameters [S1].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family rely on the differentiability of the forward projection operator $\mathcal{P}$ and its adjoint ([back-projection](#2450-back-projection.md)) $\mathcal{P}^T$ [G]. The core optimization problem is generally formulated as minimizing a loss function $\mathcal{L}$ between the measured sinogram $p$ and the rendered projection $\hat{p} = \mathcal{P}(x)$ of the current volume estimate $x$:

$$
\min_x \mathcal{L}(\mathcal{P}(x), p) + \lambda R(x)
$$

where $R(x)$ is a regularizer (e.g., Total Variation, neural prior) and $\lambda$ is a weighting factor [S1, unofficial][S2].

The gradient of the loss with respect to the volume $x$ is computed via the chain rule:

$$
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial x} = \mathcal{P}^T \left( \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial \hat{p}} \right)
$$

The term $\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial \hat{p}}$ is the residual gradient in projection space (e.g., $p - \hat{p}$ for MSE), and $\mathcal{P}^T$ is the back-projection operator [G].

Key shared components include:
1.  **Forward Projection:** [Ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) through the volume representation (voxels, octrees, or neural fields) to compute line integrals of density/absorption coefficients [S1, unofficial].
2.  **[Backward Projection](#1491-backward-projection.md) (Adjoint):** Distributing the error from the 2D detector plane back into the 3D volume. This is mathematically the transpose of the forward operator, ensuring stable convergence in iterative methods [G].
3.  **Optimization Loop:** An iterative process (e.g., SGD, Adam) that updates the volume parameters (voxel values, neural network weights, or Gaussian parameters) to reduce the projection error [S1, unofficial][S2].

## Subtopics

### [Neural Adaptive Tomography (NeAT)](1862-neural-adaptive-tomography-neat.md)
NeAT uses a hybrid explicit-implicit structure, combining an adaptive octree with neural feature grids stored in leaf nodes. It is chosen for sparse-view or limited-angle tomography where traditional methods fail, as it simultaneously optimizes the [volume, camera](#4116-volume-visualization-camera.md) poses, and photometric parameters (reference image). It outperforms purely [implicit methods](#12421-implicit-methods-sdf-based.md) in compute time for scattered samples.

### [HoloINR](4745-holoinr.md)
[HoloINR](#4745-holoinr.md) solves near-field holotomography by explicitly modeling Fresnel propagation physics between the object and detector, rather than assuming far-field propagation. It is chosen when near-field diffraction effects are significant, mapping 3D coordinates to complex-valued scattering potentials.

### [Canonical Neural Radiance Field for X-ray Tomography](11451-canonical-neural-radiance-field-for-x-ray-tomography.md)
This method decouples the static canonical volume from the [deformation field](#13852-deformation-field-modeling.md), using rich static projections to train the volume and sparse dynamic projections to learn motion. It is chosen for [dynamic tomography](#7376-dynamic-tomographic-reconstruction-with-motion-identificatio.md) to avoid the poor performance of directly inputting time into conventional NeRFs.

### [VolumeNeRF](13110-volumenerf.md)
[VolumeNeRF](#13110-volumenerf.md) reconstructs 3D CT volumes from a single 2D [X-ray projection](#1492-forward-projection-atx.md) by integrating anatomical priors (Mean CT and Likelihood Images) via Projection Attention Modules (PAMs). It is chosen for single-view reconstruction to mitigate ill-posedness using structural priors.

## Background
The application of [Neural Radiance Fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) ([NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md)) to X-ray tomography emerged from the success of NeRF in novel view synthesis for visible light [S1, unofficial]. Traditional iterative reconstruction methods (e.g., [SIRT](#3101-sirt-simultaneous-iterative-reconstruction-technique.md), FDK) struggle with sparse data and noise [S1]. Neural inverse rendering methods were developed to leverage the continuous nature of INRs for higher resolution and robustness in ill-posed scenarios [S1, unofficial].
